thread:
ani_java: heads-up: ran into a weird onboarding failure in the sampleapp when using the Java SDK with default prefetch=4. auth retry + pagination caused either long stalls or sudden bursts of Generate calls.
sam_dotnet: same pattern reported by a customer on .NET. are we seeing connection_pool exhaustion or backend 429s?
ani_java: both depending on timing. java token refresh blocks caller thread, pager keeps prefetching pages, then when refresh returns the backlog floods the client -> transient 429s. sometimes threads block and onboarding hangs.
toni_swe: can you paste the minimal snippet?
ani_java: ```java
for (Page page : pager) {
  client.generate(page.items()); // may call TokenManager.refresh() which blocks on HTTP call
}
```
lee_devx: JS/Go/py behave differently because their refresh path yields; looks like an SDK parity gap.
sam_dotnet: quick mitigation options: lower sampleapp prefetch default, make token refresh async-yielding, or make pager pause when auth refresh is in-flight.
ani_java: I tried forcing pager.setPrefetch(1) in the sampleapp and the problem went away for onboarding. but that's not ideal for perf.
toni_swe: suggestion: add a lightweight backpressure hook in SDK that detects auth-refresh and temporarily reduces prefetch window to 1, with an opt-out flag. also add a small yield after refresh in Java to hand off work to executor.
lee_devx: please add a tiny repro in sampleapp and a README troubleshooting note. we'll want an integration test that simulates flaky STS (socket reset) and asserts no backlog > limit.
ci-bot: created issue DEVEX-1239 "sdk-prefetch-auth-backpressure" and attached logs.
ani_java: ok i'll open a PR to: 1) lower sampleapp prefetch to 1 by default, 2) add the repro and README, 3) implement opt-in auth-yield behavior in Java SDK. tagging @sam_dotnet for parity plan.
sam_dotnet: i'll mirror the Java change in dotnet and add a test in CI.
